title: Lian Po Carries Thorns to Lin Xiangru
text:
In the 3rd century BC, in the kingdom of Zhao, Lian Po was a famous general. Lin Xiangru had begun as a household retainer, but he twice outfaced the powerful king of Qin in diplomacy, once by bringing the precious He jade back safely and once at the meeting at Mianchi. King Huiwen rewarded him with a rank above Lian Po.

Sima Qian records that Lian Po was furious. He had won his rank fighting, he said, while this upstart had only used his tongue, and he swore to humiliate Lin if they met. Lin Xiangru avoided him. He pleaded illness to skip court, and once turned his carriage aside when he saw Lian Po coming. His own followers felt ashamed and wanted to leave him.

Lin explained that he had not feared the king of Qin, so he did not fear Lian Po. But Qin left Zhao alone only because the two of them were there; if they fought, Qin would profit. He put the state first and private grudges last. When Lian Po heard this, he bared his back, carried a bundle of thorny branches, and went to Lin's gate to beg punishment. The two became friends ready to die for each other.
lesson: When a rival attacks your pride, ask what the fight would cost the people you both serve. And when you realize you were wrong, apologize openly and in person.
people: Lian Po, Lin Xiangru, King Huiwen of Zhao
location: Handan, State of Zhao (modern Hebei, China)
source: Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), chapter 81, Biographies of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru
